source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW) for the Management of Acute Diarrhea
source.publisher: Department of Health Research, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India

condition_description: Diarrhea means three or more loose or watery stools per day. Acute diarrhea lasts less than 14 days. Diarrhea lasting more than 14 days is persistent diarrhea. Dysentery means blood is present in the stools.

sections.label: Signs of Severe Dehydration: Go to Hospital Immediately
items: Lethargy or unconsciousness
Sunken eyes
Not able to drink at all, or drinking very poorly
Skin pinch test: pinch the skin on the abdomen, if the skin goes back very slowly (takes more than 2 seconds to flatten), this indicates severe dehydration
Very rapid or weak pulse
Very low blood pressure
Rapid breathing
Passing many watery stools very frequently with no improvement
Repeated vomiting preventing any fluid intake
Blood in stools with no improvement after 2 days of treatment
Diarrhea with high fever and worsening general condition
Diarrhea in a person with severe malnutrition or known HIV
Persistent diarrhea lasting more than 14 days with signs of dehydration or serious illness

sections.label: Self-Care at Home: Fluid Replacement is the Most Important Step
items: Start oral rehydration immediately, the most important treatment for diarrhea at home is replacing lost fluids and salts

Use ORS (Oral Rehydration Salt) sachets available at any pharmacy or government health centre: dissolve one sachet in the amount of clean water shown on the packet (usually 200 ml or 1 litre) and sip frequently
If ORS sachets are not available, a homemade alternative can be used temporarily: add a pinch of salt and a small amount of sugar to a glass of clean water, stir well, and sip frequently
Other suitable homemade fluids: salted rice water, salted yogurt drink (lassi with salt), vegetable or chicken soup with salt, unsweetened fresh fruit juice, coconut water
Give extra fluids after each loose stool, adults should drink at least 200 ml after each episode
Unsuitable fluids that worsen diarrhea: carbonated beverages (cold drinks/soda), commercial sweetened fruit juices, sweetened tea or coffee
Continue eating, do not fast. Eat light, easily digestible foods. Avoid oily or spicy food during illness
Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water before eating, after using the toilet, and after handling stool
Use clean, safe drinking water only, boil water if safety is uncertain
Return for medical attention immediately if: passing many watery stools, repeatedly vomiting, unable to drink, developing fever, noticing blood in stool, or condition is not improving in 5 days

sections.label: See a Doctor
items: Diarrhea not improving after 5 days of home management
Any blood in the stools (dysentery)
Significant vomiting along with diarrhea making it hard to keep fluids down
Signs of moderate dehydration: restlessness, sunken eyes, feeling very thirsty, skin pinch goes back slowly
Fever along with diarrhea
Diarrhea in a person with diabetes, heart disease, or kidney disease
Diarrhea lasting more than 14 days (persistent diarrhea)
Diarrhea after travel to a new place or after eating outside food with suspected contamination

sections.label: Go to Hospital Without Delay
items: Any sign of severe dehydration listed above, unconsciousness, unable to drink, skin pinch very slow, very weak pulse
Blood in stools with no improvement after 2 days of treatment
Persistent diarrhea (more than 14 days) with dehydration or serious infection signs
Diarrhea with severe vomiting and complete inability to keep fluids down
Suspected cholera: sudden onset of very profuse watery diarrhea (rice-water stool), especially in an area with known cholera

dehydration_assessment.label: Simple Home Dehydration Check (Skin Pinch Test)
dehydration_assessment.description: Pinch the skin on the abdomen between two fingers, hold for one second, then let go. Watch how quickly it returns to normal: if it goes back immediately, no significant dehydration; if it stays raised for a brief instant, some dehydration, needs ORS urgently; if it goes back very slowly, taking more than 2 seconds, severe dehydration, go to hospital immediately.

review.notes: All antibiotic names, IV fluid regimens, drug dosing, and lab investigation thresholds excluded. ORS preparation instructions retained as these are non-drug public health measures essential for safe home management. The dehydration skin pinch test is included as a self-assessment tool directly from the source document, it requires no drug or clinical knowledge to apply.
